title: P42: independently orthogonal Q, K and V initialization
description: P42 follow-up: initialize each Q/K/V 256-by-256 matrix independently and orthogonally at gain 0.32, instead of jointly orthogonalizing their 768-by-256 concatenation. Matching the independent roles used by the incumbent Muon updates may improve the proof policy handed to fixed downstream expert iteration.
hypothesis: Incumbent 043 orthogonal initialization scored 282/275/269 (exact mean 275.333333), a modest mixed-seed gain over 040. Its joint QKV orthogonality constrains the sum of Q/K/V Gram matrices but does not make each role well-conditioned. Independent square orthogonal initialization gives each role equal singular values while preserving exact mean squared elements at 0.0004, potentially improving early attention and value signal propagation and downstream proof discovery. Run 031 split Muon updates, not initialization; no prior record tests this initializer split, and the other agent's 044 tests attention gates. All other hidden matrices keep their incumbent initialization, and no architecture or optimizer rule changes. This is not proof that conditioning is a bottleneck; useful anisotropy or joint geometry may be lost. Initial random draws and RNG trajectories may differ with decomposition/backend, while the seed policy and separately seeded data generator stay fixed. Expect negligible steady-state latency change and less than one second initialization difference within the existing budget. Only the downstream three-seed mean decides keep/discard.
expected_delta: +3 to +12 dev-transfer theorems at true length >=7 in the three-seed mean; plausible negative outcome if joint geometry is useful

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon hidden matrices throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 16 hidden projection parameters remain in Muon. Four qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 remain unchanged.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, head.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters throughout; hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Muon lr*0.01 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, preserving incumbent per-update shrinkage at every schedule fraction, including the former finish window; integrated decay can differ with throughput.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Fork default construction, then orthogonal initialization after moving to device. Each of four qkv.weight (768,256) matrices is chunked along rows into Q/K/V (256,256), each independently orthogonal_ with gain 0.02*sqrt(256)=0.32. Remaining proj (256,256), fc1 (1024,256), fc2 (256,1024) initialized exactly as incumbent with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows,columns)). All hidden matrices have exact element second moment 0.0004. Embedding, readout, biases and LayerNorm retain their original fork values. No reinitialization during RL.
